targets.label: SSH Weak KEX + DSA Host Key

findings.title: TLS 1.0 Detected
findings.description: TLS 1.0 is deprecated and contains known vulnerabilities (BEAST, POODLE). It is prohibited by BSI TR-02102-2 and eIDAS 2.0.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to TLS 1.2 (minimum) or TLS 1.3. Disable TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 in server configuration.

findings.title: RC4 Cipher Suite Detected
findings.description: RC4 is a broken stream cipher with multiple known vulnerabilities (BEAST, RC4 biases). Its use is prohibited.
findings.remediation: Disable RC4 cipher suites. Use ECDHE with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

findings.title: RSA Key Too Short (512 bits)
findings.description: RSA-512 key is cryptographically weak and can be factored with modern hardware. Minimum acceptable is RSA-2048.
findings.remediation: Replace certificate with RSA-3072 or higher (BSI recommends RSA-3072 for post-2022 use).

findings.title: SHA-1 Certificate Signature
findings.description: SHA-1 is deprecated for certificate signing. Practical collision attacks have been demonstrated (SHAttered). Browsers reject SHA-1 certificates.
findings.remediation: Re-issue certificate using SHA-256 or SHA-384 signature algorithm.

findings.target_label: SSH Weak KEX + DSA Host Key
findings.title: CRITICAL: Oakley Group 1 (768-bit DH) KEX Detected
findings.description: diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 uses 768-bit Diffie-Hellman (Oakley Group 1) which is trivially breakable with modern hardware (Logjam attack).
findings.remediation: Remove weak KEX algorithms from sshd_config. Use curve25519-sha256 or diffie-hellman-group16-sha512.

findings.title: TLS 1.2 Without Forward Secrecy
findings.description: TLS 1.2 is in use but the negotiated cipher suite does not provide forward secrecy (no ECDHE/DHE key exchange).
findings.remediation: Configure cipher suite preference to require ECDHE or DHE key exchange for forward secrecy.

findings.title: RSA-2048 Key (Upgrade Recommended)
findings.description: RSA-2048 meets current minimums but BSI TR-02102-1 recommends RSA-3072 or higher for long-term security beyond 2025.
findings.remediation: Plan migration to RSA-3072 or ECDSA-P-256/P-384 for better performance and longer security horizon.

findings.title: TLS 1.2 Best Practice: Prefer TLS 1.3
findings.description: While TLS 1.2 is acceptable, TLS 1.3 provides improved security and performance with mandatory forward secrecy.
findings.remediation: Configure the server to prefer TLS 1.3 and restrict TLS 1.2 to approved cipher suites only.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Strict-Transport-Security Header
findings.description: The Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header is absent, allowing potential protocol downgrade attacks.
findings.remediation: Add 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload' to all HTTPS responses.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options Header
findings.description: The X-Content-Type-Options header is missing. This can allow MIME-sniffing attacks.
findings.remediation: Add 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' to all HTTP responses.

findings.title: Missing X-Frame-Options Header
findings.description: The X-Frame-Options header is missing, which may allow clickjacking attacks.
findings.remediation: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN' to all HTTP responses.

findings.target_label: SSH Weak KEX + DSA Host Key
findings.title: DSA Host Key Detected
findings.description: DSA (Digital Signature Algorithm) is limited to 1024-bit keys and is considered cryptographically weak. It is deprecated in OpenSSH.
findings.remediation: Replace DSA host keys with Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256. Add 'HostKeyAlgorithms -ssh-dss' to sshd_config.
